body: Sony is bringing **AI-guided upscaling** to the standard PlayStation 5, and that makes QSSR one of the most important PS5 platform updates of the year.

The feature is called **Quick Spectral Super Resolution**, or **QSSR**. Sony describes it as a new performance tier of AI upscaling for the base PS5, while **PSSR** remains the higher-end PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution path for PS5 Pro.
That distinction matters because this is not Sony erasing the value of PS5 Pro. It is Sony trying to bring a lighter version of the same image-quality idea to the much larger standard PS5 audience.
## What QSSR Actually Is
QSSR is designed to improve image detail and image stability on the standard PS5 by using a streamlined neural-network approach tuned for the base console.

The consumer takeaway is simple: this is not just a PS5 Pro trick anymore. More PS5 owners may start seeing games render internally at a lower or more flexible resolution, then reconstruct a cleaner final image than older upscaling methods could provide.
## QSSR vs PSSR

body: ## Why This Matters for Players

The biggest win is not a spec-sheet talking point. It is flexibility. Developers often have to decide between resolution, frame rate, ray tracing, world density, effects, and image stability. A better upscaler can give them more room to hit a stable performance target without making the final image look soft or unstable.

For players, that could mean performance modes that look cleaner, fidelity modes that hold together better in motion, or games that avoid some of the shimmer and blur associated with older reconstruction methods.

body: ## The First Supported Games Matter

Sony says the first titles to use QSSR are **Marvel's Wolverine** and **Ghost of Yotei**. That matters because the announcement is not an abstract technology promise. It starts with two highly visible PlayStation games.

Those are exactly the kinds of titles where image reconstruction gets tested hard: character detail, open environments, motion, lighting, particle effects, and camera movement. If QSSR holds up there, it becomes much easier to imagine the feature becoming normal across future PS5 releases.
## What We Know

* QSSR is coming to the base PS5
* Sony says it uses AI-guided upscaling principles
* PSSR remains tied to PS5 Pro as the premium path
* Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei are the first announced QSSR titles
* Sony plans to offer QSSR broadly to PlayStation developers
* PlayStation's earlier PSSR posts show Sony has been steadily expanding its AI-upscaling work across PS5 Pro games
## What We Still Need to See

* direct side-by-side image-quality comparisons
* how QSSR behaves across performance and fidelity modes
* whether existing PS5 games receive patches
* how broad adoption becomes across first-party and third-party releases
* whether developers expose QSSR clearly in graphics menus or simply make it part of default modes
## GCX Takeaway
The most exciting part is not just that PS5 is getting a new graphics option. It is that Sony is making AI upscaling a platform feature for the console most players already own.

The cautious read is just as important: QSSR is not PSSR magically transplanted into every base PS5 game overnight. It needs developer support, game-by-game tuning, and real comparisons before players know how much difference it makes. But if Sony gets this right, QSSR could make the late PS5 generation feel cleaner and more flexible without requiring a Pro upgrade.

body: **Gears of War: E-Day** is now in early access, which means the conversation has finally moved out of trailer speculation and into the hands of players. Premium Edition owners and eligible Game Pass players who bought the Premium Upgrade can play before the full worldwide launch on **October 6, 2026**.

That access split is the whole point of this hub. A lot of players are not asking whether E-Day exists. They are asking whether they can play today, whether Game Pass is enough, what the Premium Upgrade actually unlocks, and what modes are available once they get in. This hub answers those questions cleanly without making people decode three store pages and a launch post.
## Launch Timing and Access

body.caption: Xbox and The Coalition separate early access from the full Game Pass launch. This is the cleanest way to read the week.
rows: When did early access start?
October 1, 2026 at 8:00 a.m. PT / 15:00 UTC.
If you have the right edition or upgrade, the early-access window is already active.
When is the full launch?
October 6, 2026 at 8:00 a.m. PT / 15:00 UTC.
This is the standard launch date and the day-one Game Pass date.
Is Game Pass alone enough for October 1?
No. Xbox says day-one Game Pass access begins October 6; early access is for Premium Edition players and Game Pass subscribers with the Premium Upgrade.
This is the access detail most likely to confuse players, so it belongs in plain language.
What platforms are covered?
Xbox Series X|S, Windows PC, Steam, and cloud through Game Pass Ultimate and GeForce NOW.
The audience is broader than console-only Gears fans, especially with Steam and cloud in the mix.

body: The important distinction is that **Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass get the game on October 6**, while the **Premium Edition** and **Premium Edition Upgrade** add up to five days of early access. Xbox's product page also lists Standard Edition at $69.99, Premium Edition at $99.99, and a $30 Premium Edition Upgrade for players who already own the base game.

That means a Game Pass subscriber who wants to play during early access should be looking at the Premium Upgrade path, not assuming the subscription by itself unlocks October 1. Xbox also notes the upgrade requires the base game or a Game Pass Ultimate membership, sold separately.
## What Early Access Actually Includes

body.caption: E-Day is not only a campaign launch. The official product copy and multiplayer deep dive point to campaign, Horde Siege, and Versus as the launch-week pillars.
headers: What Xbox or The Coalition says
rows: Campaign
Set fourteen years before the original Gears of War, following Marcus Fenix and Dominic Santiago during the first days of the Locust invasion.
This is the emotional hook: E-Day is a prequel about the moment the world breaks, not just another sequel escalation.
Co-op
Campaign supports solo play, two-player split-screen on console, and up to four players online.
Split-screen being console-only is worth calling out before players make couch co-op plans.
Horde Siege
A reimagined PvE mode with four-player squads, larger maps, objectives, classes, extraction, weapon parts, and world-boss-style events.
This is the long-tail co-op lane and probably where launch-week groups will spend a lot of time after campaign sessions.
Versus
Four-versus-four PvP launches with Team Deathmatch, Conquest, Demolition, Crucible, six new maps, Ranked, Social, and bot/practice paths.
The Coalition is trying to keep classic Gears tension while making onboarding less brutal for new or rusty players.
Customization
The Coalition says nearly every customization item can be earned by playing, with exceptions for Premium Edition content, charity offers, and crossover bundles.
That messaging matters because live-service fatigue is real; players want to know whether progression respects their time.

body: The gameplay pitch is also clearer now. The Coalition says E-Day was built from scratch to "feel like Gears but play like new," with rebuilt cover systems, more deliberate movement, simulated projectile ballistics, weapon tweaks, and a renewed focus on Locust threat readability. That is not just marketing texture; it is the exact design problem Gears has to solve.

If E-Day gets too loose, it stops feeling like Gears. If it gets too nostalgic, it risks feeling stuck. The most interesting launch-week question is whether the new movement, cover, weapon, and enemy work can modernize the series without sanding off its heavy, ugly, intimate combat rhythm.

body: ## What the Game Is About

E-Day goes back to **Emergence Day**, the catastrophic beginning of the Locust invasion. The story focuses on a younger **Marcus Fenix** and **Dom Santiago**, turning the series into a prequel about panic, horror, and survival before the franchise's heroes became legends.

That framing gives The Coalition a useful reset. The Locust are not familiar targets yet. Civilians do not understand what is happening. The COG is reacting to a disaster in real time. If the campaign lands, E-Day can make the franchise feel dangerous again instead of simply larger.

The launch trailer leans into that exact mood, using Metallica's **For Whom the Bell Tolls** over the return to Emergence Day. It is a very Gears choice: blunt, huge, and not remotely subtle. Sometimes that is the correct tool.
## GCX Takeaway

E-Day is the kind of launch that deserves a living Xbox hub, not a disposable news hit. It has a clear access question, a major Game Pass angle, a franchise-history hook, and enough multiplayer detail to keep readers coming back after they finish the campaign.

The useful promise here is simple: tell players whether they can play, what they are getting, what mode they should try first, and where to check if something breaks. That practical layer becomes more valuable every time launch-week confusion spikes.

body: The October wave of **Pokemon TCG: 30th Celebration** products is live, and it gives collectors several new ways to open or display the anniversary set without jumping straight to the biggest boxed products.

The headliners are the **Booster Bundle** and **Mini Tins**, but the October 2 lineup also includes the Enhanced 2-Pack Blister and Mini Portfolio. The practical question is not only what comes in each product. It is which one actually fits what a collector is trying to do: open packs, chase promos, build a display row, or keep sealed product clean for later.

Pokemon has also framed 30th Celebration as a set built around anniversary nostalgia, Mewtwo ex and Mew ex, popular allies, and 30 Pikachu rare cards, so the October products are not isolated accessories. They are another way into the core anniversary chase.

body: ## Booster Bundle

The **Booster Bundle** is the cleanest pack-opening product in this wave: six 30th Celebration booster packs and no extra accessories to price into the decision. If your goal is simply to open the anniversary set, this is the easiest product to compare against any other sealed option.

That also means it may be one of the first products buyers use to judge real demand. If Booster Bundles disappear faster than accessory-heavy products, that usually says collectors are valuing pack access over shelf extras.
## Mini Tins

The **Mini Tins** are the visual star of the October 2 wave. Pokemon says there are **10 different designs**, and the artwork can be combined to form two large images: one day-themed and one night-themed.

Each tin includes two 30th Celebration booster packs, a sticker sheet, and a Pokemon art card matching the tin design. That makes the Mini Tin line a hybrid product: part pack purchase, part display chase, part low-cost sealed collectible.
## Enhanced 2-Pack Blister

The Enhanced 2-Pack Blister adds a foil promo card and coin to the two-pack format. Pokemon's October product page highlights Gengar, Marshadow, and Team Rocket's Mimikyu as featured foil-card possibilities.

This is the product to watch if promo demand starts driving prices separately from pack demand. A blister can look modest on release day, then become the thing collectors remember if one of its featured cards becomes the chase.
## Mini Portfolio
The Mini Portfolio is the small binder option. It comes with one booster pack and gives newer collectors an easy place to start storing favorite pulls from the anniversary set.
It is not the most pack-efficient product, but it has a clear audience: younger collectors, gift buyers, and anyone who wants a low-friction accessory rather than another box for the sealed pile.

body: ## Availability Notes

Pokemon's official October product roundup lists the Booster Bundle and Mini Tin as October 2 releases. Pokemon Center support also lists 30th Celebration Booster Bundles and Mini Tins in its estimated preorder release-date table, with US, Canada, and UK timing shown around early October or late October depending on the listing group.

That is why GCX is treating this as a living product hub rather than a one-and-done announcement. The contents are official, but availability can change by retailer, region, allocation, and restock timing.
## What We Know

* the products launch in the October 2026 wave
* Booster Bundles include 6 packs
* Mini Tins come in 10 designs
* each Mini Tin includes 2 packs, stickers, and an art card

* Mini Portfolios include 1 pack and a mini binder
* Pokemon Center lists Booster Bundles and Mini Tins in its preorder release-date support table
## GCX Takeaway

This is the most collector-friendly 30th Celebration wave so far because each product has a clear job. Booster Bundles are for opening packs, Mini Tins are for display and set building, Blisters add promo value, and Mini Portfolios give newer collectors a simple place to keep the cards they pull.

The best version of this page is not just a product list. It should keep helping readers decide what to buy, what to open, and what to watch as official availability and retailer stock settle after launch.

body: **Reality Fracture** is no longer just the next Magic: The Gathering set on the calendar. It is Wizards of the Coast turning Jace Beleren's Echoverse idea into a full launch moment: cards, products, store events, Arena timing, Commander hooks, and enough collector treatments to make even casual Magic fans ask what exactly broke.

For GCX, this is the kind of Magic story that deserves a durable hub instead of a quick headline. Pokemon coverage can still be a major strength, but Reality Fracture gives the card side of the site a different flavor: one part story climax, one part booster-fun checklist, one part local-store event calendar.
## Reality Fracture At a Glance

body: The short version: Reality Fracture is a set about the cost of Jace trying to solve the Multiverse by replacing it. The product page frames the launch around a reality where Jace's plan worked and the consequences are now everybody else's problem.

That gives the set a cleaner identity than a normal seasonal release. You do not need to know every recent Magic story beat to understand why the visuals land. The appeal is seeing the familiar Multiverse through a wrong mirror: alternate Chandra, alternate Ajani, alternate Karn, and a tower full of Jace logic that absolutely nobody should trust without reading the fine print.
## Collector Treatments to Watch

body.caption: Reality Fracture's major collector hooks are not all the same product chase. Some are broad set identity; some are Collector Booster-specific.
rows: Echoed pairs
Every Play Booster and Collector Booster contains echoed pairs. Wizards lists 66 uncommon, 14 rare, and 6 mythic rare individual echoed-pair cards.
This is the set's main identity, not just a premium chase. It is the best shorthand for the Echoverse concept.
Borderless echoed pairs
Two-card borderless scenes show characters and counterparts clashing across realities, with non-foil and traditional foil versions in Play and Collector Boosters.
These are the binder-page cards casual collectors will understand immediately because the art literally spans the conflict.
Shattered mirror cards
Rare and mythic rare alternate-path cards appear in Play and Collector Boosters; facet foil versions are Collector Booster-only and always English.
This is the premium chase lane. Foil language and approximate print-volume notes matter because they affect collecting behavior.
Special Guests panorama
Ten Special Guests cards form a wraparound Echoverse panorama illustrated by Marina Banker.
This is the display-set hook: less about a single chase card and more about completing a visual scene.
Secret Lair Bundle
The Reality Fracture Secret Lair Bundle combines set product with exclusive Secret Lair-style promo treatments.
This creates a separate collector path from normal boxes, especially for players who care about treatment exclusivity.

body: The most important thing for readers is that Reality Fracture has multiple collector lanes. Echoed pairs explain the set. Shattered mirror cards drive the premium hunt. Special Guests give completionists a panorama project. The Secret Lair Bundle creates a product-specific promo path. Those should not be flattened into one vague phrase like "new variants."
## Mechanics and Play Identity

Reality Fracture also has a mechanical identity beyond the card treatments. Wizards highlights **empower Jace** as the marquee keyword action. In practice, that means cards can create or grow a blue Jace planeswalker token, giving the set a literal board-state expression of Jace inserting himself into everything. It is funny, ominous, and extremely on brand.

The mechanics article also calls out **Heartwood tokens**, a new predefined token type that produces red or green mana, and the return of **prepare** cards, which split creature bodies and spell options across the card frame. That matters because the set is not only selling alternate-reality art. It is also asking players to manage extra objects, modes, and resource lines in games.

For newer or returning players, the practical takeaway is simple: Reality Fracture may read busy at first. Learn the Jace token flow, pay attention to which cards are echoed pairs, and treat prerelease as a good place to see how the mechanics actually feel before buying hard into a constructed deck idea.

Townfall is set on **St. Amelia**, a cold, isolated Scottish island wrapped in fog, silence, and fragments of memory. Konami describes Simon Ordell as an outsider who has washed onto the marina of St. Amelia, where the presence of former residents still lingers.

That setting gives Townfall a different shape from Silent Hill 2, Silent Hill f, and the original town mythology. It still looks like Silent Hill in mood, but it is not relying only on old geography to earn that name.
## Why First Person Matters

The first-person shift changes the contract between player and horror. Classic Silent Hill often used distance: a character framed in the environment, the camera holding tension, the player watching dread close in. Townfall removes much of that buffer.

Sony's feature coverage frames the perspective as a way to make exploration, puzzle-solving, evasion, combat, and uncertainty feel more immediate. Instead of watching Simon move through St. Amelia, players inhabit the space where the sound, fog, and unreliable signals are pointed directly at them.

Konami has described Townfall as a full-length, self-contained psychological horror game, and the design language appears to lean as hard on atmosphere and puzzles as it does on direct confrontation.
The CRTV pocket television is central to that identity. It is not just flavor dressing for a retro mood; it is tied to clues, unstable signals, and the layered reality of St. Amelia.

body: Undead Labs is independent again, but State of Decay 3 has not disappeared from the Xbox roadmap.

The studio announced on September 22, 2026 that it completed its separation from Xbox and is now operating as an independent, employee-owned developer. On the same day, Xbox Wire said Undead Labs had transitioned out of Microsoft ownership and that State of Decay 3 will still release day one on Game Pass with a new publisher.
That combination is the important part. The corporate owner changed. The announced game plan did not suddenly reset.

For players, this is less a cancellation scare and more a publishing-watch story: State of Decay 3 is still targeted for 2027, still in active development, still tied to Game Pass, and still planned across Xbox, PC, Steam, and PlayStation. The unresolved question is how the new publishing structure will be presented once store pages, trailers, and future beta updates are refreshed.
## Undead Labs Leaves Xbox

Undead Labs says the separation is complete after a Microsoft relationship that goes back more than 15 years. The first State of Decay launched with Microsoft in 2013, and Microsoft acquired the Seattle-area studio in 2018 after State of Decay 2 had already made the franchise a meaningful part of the Xbox survival catalog.

The 2026 move reverses that ownership structure without ending the franchise relationship outright. Xbox described Undead Labs as part of a broader studio-divestiture plan that also included Compulsion and Double Fine returning to management with IP, back catalogs, and runway funding.

That phrasing matters because it suggests Microsoft is trying to keep some strategic games moving while owning fewer studios directly. It also leaves room for the new Undead Labs to keep building the game with a publishing partner rather than starting over from a cold stop.
## State of Decay 3 Is Still Coming to Game Pass

Undead Labs says development of State of Decay 3 remains actively underway. The studio also says the game is currently in alpha, still moving toward the previously announced closed-beta milestone before the end of 2026, and still targeted for release in 2027 on Xbox, Game Pass, PC, and PlayStation.
Xbox Wire goes one step further on the Game Pass point: Microsoft says the game will release day one on Game Pass with a new publisher.

The current Xbox product page continues to reinforce the same consumer-facing promise. It lists State of Decay 3 as available in 2027, highlights day-one Game Pass, identifies Undead Labs as the developer, and shows Xbox Play Anywhere support. It also lists Xbox Series X and S and Windows PC in the details while the broader ways-to-play section includes Steam and PlayStation branding.
That does not mean every business detail is public. It means the player-facing commitments still line up across the official sources as of this update.

There is one interesting wrinkle: the Xbox product page still lists Xbox Game Studios as publisher even though Xbox Wire says State of Decay 3 will launch with a new publisher.

That is not automatically a contradiction. Store metadata often lags behind corporate updates, especially during restructuring. But it is exactly the kind of thing worth tracking because publisher labels affect player expectations around cross-play, support, marketing, release timing, and future content.

If the product page changes from Xbox Game Studios to a new publisher, that will be a meaningful update. If it does not change, the next Xbox or Undead Labs statement should clarify how the new publisher arrangement works.
## Why This Matters Beyond One Zombie Game
State of Decay 3 is now one of the clearest tests of Xbox’s post-reset studio model.

If the game launches on schedule, keeps its Game Pass commitment, and expands to PlayStation while Undead Labs operates independently, it gives Microsoft a template for supporting important franchises without directly owning every studio behind them.
If the publishing transition creates delays, confused messaging, or reduced support, it becomes a warning sign for other Xbox-linked projects leaving first-party ownership.

Either way, the key lesson is that ownership and platform availability are no longer the same question. Undead Labs can be independent while State of Decay 3 remains connected to Xbox through Game Pass, store presence, playtesting, and publishing agreements.

That gives Dual Override an immediate source of replayability if stages and bosses feel meaningfully different depending on which character you choose.
## Official Trailer

Capcom's Gamescom trailer is the source of the major gameplay beats here. Games Exchange links the official press source and will add the trailer embed when the approved publisher upload is available.
## Custom Chips Let You Build Your Own Mega Man
The new **Custom Chip** system lets players modify and enhance abilities. Capcom's reveal showed examples such as rapid-fire shots, a protective shield bubble and hover capability.
Rather than every player experiencing Mega Man in exactly the same way, Dual Override appears to let players build around preferred movement and combat styles.
## Override Is Powerful - and Deliberately Dangerous
The system that gives the game its name is **Override**. Activating it temporarily removes a robot's normal limiter, allowing Mega Man or Proto Man to unleash far more power.

There is a catch: when Override ends, several abilities temporarily stop functioning. That creates a classic risk-reward decision: use it too early and leave yourself vulnerable, or hold it too long and waste the opportunity.
## What Gamescom Revealed

* Proto Man is playable
* Custom Chips modify abilities
* Override temporarily boosts power
* Override causes temporary performance penalties afterward
* New Robot Master: Twinkle Girl

* 2027 release window

## Meet Twinkle Girl

Gamescom also introduced a new Robot Master: **Twinkle Girl**. Capcom describes her as an energetic performer whose nighttime show goes out of control, turning her firework displays into a threat Mega Man has to stop.
## Astro Man Is Back Too
Longtime fans may have noticed **Astro Man**, originally introduced in Mega Man 8. Capcom has not explained exactly what his role is or whether other classic Robot Masters will return.
## The Platform List Is Huge
Mega Man: Dual Override is scheduled for **2027** on Nintendo Switch 2, Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, Xbox on PC, Steam and Epic Games Store.
## Why This One Matters
Mega Man has survived for decades partly because the core formula is so clean: run, jump, shoot, learn the boss, steal the power.
The danger in modernizing that is obvious. Add too many systems and you bury what makes Mega Man work. Add too little and the game risks feeling like a nostalgia exercise.
Custom Chips and Override are interesting because they sit directly on top of the old formula rather than replacing it. That is probably the right place to experiment.

body: The biggest compliment you can probably give **Gears of War: E-Day** after its Gamescom campaign debut is also the simplest: it feels like Gears.
The Coalition's prequel appears deliberately built around the weight, brutality and claustrophobic combat that made the first game feel so different in 2006.
## This Is the First Public Campaign Hands-On
Gamescom 2026 marks the first time the public can play the E-Day campaign. The demo takes place during the early hours after the Locust erupt onto the surface of Sera.
Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago are joined by two new squadmates, **Lucas Reyes and Mags Carter**, as Bravo Squad tries to survive the first chaos of Emergence Day in the city of Kalona.
The story unfolds across three nights, long before Marcus and Dom become the legends players know from the original trilogy.
## Official Gameplay

## The Cover System Still Has Weight

One of the defining details in Xbox's hands-on coverage is how familiar movement feels. Marcus still slams into cover. Weapons still feel heavy. Combat still emphasizes positioning rather than turning the game into a hyper-mobile shooter.
That matters because Gears has always been at its best when every movement feels slightly dangerous.
## The Horror Is Back
The Coalition has repeatedly said E-Day is meant to recover more of the horror that defined the original Gears. Gamescom impressions suggest that is not just marketing language.

The Locust are new to the characters. Nobody understands what they are. Civilians are panicking. Military leadership is improvising. That uncertainty gives the Locust something later games could never fully recreate: mystery.
## Marcus and Dom Are Younger - But Not Unrecognizable

E-Day takes place **14 years before the original Gears of War**. The game focuses on the beginning of Marcus and Dom's bond and the experience that transforms them into the soldiers players already know.
## What Gamescom Confirmed

body: # Console Sales Are Sliding - Why the Average Gaming System Now Costs $542
The console business has a new affordability problem.

Circana reporting for July 2026 shows U.S. new video game hardware unit sales down **39% year over year**, while the average selling price of a new hardware unit rose **16% to $542**. Hardware dollar spending fell 29% to $282 million, the weakest July hardware-spending result since 2020.
That sounds like a collapse story. It is more complicated than that.

July 2025 was an unusually hard comparison because it came during the early Switch 2 launch window. Switch 2 is also still reportedly ahead of the original Switch on a time-aligned U.S. installed-base basis. So the right conclusion is not that console gaming is dying.
The sharper story is this: **fewer U.S. systems are selling while the average price buyers pay is rising sharply.** That is a dangerous combination for a hardware market built on scale.
## The July Snapshot

body: The unit decline is the headline. The ASP is the warning light.

Historically, console hardware usually gets easier to sell as a generation matures because production improves, bundles get better, and price cuts eventually arrive. In 2026, that old pattern is under pressure.
## What $542 Actually Means
$542 is not the MSRP of "the average console." It is a transaction-weighted average selling price for new video game hardware units purchased in the U.S. during July.

That means the number can move because of bundles, premium models, product mix, promotions and manufacturer price changes. If cheaper hardware sells less frequently while premium systems carry more of the market, the average climbs.
In 2026, though, the ASP story is not just mix. There are real list-price increases behind it.
## The Price Hikes Are No Longer Isolated
Sony, Microsoft and Nintendo have all moved U.S. console pricing upward in 2026 or scheduled increases that affect the market.

The takeaway is still clear: the console market is not getting the traditional late-cycle affordability relief many buyers expect.
## Why $542 Is the Number to Watch
A $542 average does not mean every console on a shelf costs exactly $542. Average selling price can move because of bundles, premium models, product mix, retailer behavior and timing.
But the direction matters. Circana also reported a $502 average hardware selling price for May 2026, up 14% versus May 2025. July pushed the snapshot higher again.

## Memory and Storage Are Now Part of the Console Story
Microsoft has been unusually direct about why its hardware prices are moving. The company says console storage and memory costs have increased dramatically and expects further pressure into 2027.

That matters because modern consoles are not just plastic boxes and chips. Fast storage, memory capacity, cooling, controllers, licensing, tariffs, exchange rates and retailer economics all shape what a manufacturer can profitably put on shelves.

The AI data-center boom has also changed the component market around memory and storage. Even when console demand softens, manufacturers may still be competing for parts in markets where higher-margin buyers have enormous appetite.
## Why This Hurts More Than a Normal Price Increase
A normal late-generation price increase is already painful. This one lands while buyers are also dealing with expensive games, subscriptions, accessories and upgrade uncertainty.

That creates a squeeze: console makers need higher prices to protect margins, but higher prices can slow the unit volume that makes the platform attractive to publishers, retailers and accessory makers.

For collectors and used-market buyers, the effect could be different. If new hardware stays expensive, used consoles may hold value longer. That is good for sellers, frustrating for late adopters and important for a marketplace like GCX to track responsibly.
## What This Does Not Mean
This is not proof that consoles are dying.

Switch 2's 2025 launch created an unusually tough comparison. PlayStation dollar sales can rise even when units fall. Xbox hardware has a different strategic role as Microsoft leans harder into PC, cloud and Game Pass.
The problem is more specific: **the old assumption that console hardware becomes cheaper and easier to sell as a generation matures is under unusual pressure.**
## GCX Verdict
The July numbers are less about one bad month and more about a market where affordability is becoming the defining hardware question.

If console makers cannot restore the sense that new hardware is a mass-market purchase, the next wave of platform growth may depend as much on financing, used hardware, trade-in programs and bundles as it does on exclusive games.
That is why GCX will keep tracking average selling price, unit volume, official MSRP changes and the used-console market together instead of treating each as a separate story.

title: Is Pokemon Preparing to Change Traditional Turn-Based Battles?

body: # Is Pokemon Preparing to Change Traditional Turn-Based Battles?
For nearly three decades, Pokemon battles have been built around one familiar ritual: choose a move, resolve the turn, read the opponent, repeat.

That ritual is not officially going away. Game Freak has not confirmed that **Pokemon Winds** and **Pokemon Waves** are abandoning turn-based combat, and the official site for the 2027 Switch 2 RPGs does not yet identify a battle system.
But the question has become much more serious because of **Pokemon Champions**.

In a new Game Freak developer video, director Kazumasa Iwao frames Champions as a way to preserve the style of Pokemon battling longtime players know while Game Freak continues challenging itself with new ideas elsewhere. GamesRadar translated his comments as saying the long-standing battle rule could change "little by little."
The defensible read is not that turn-based Pokemon is dead. It is that Game Freak now has a cleaner way to protect traditional competitive play while allowing future RPGs to experiment.
## The Short Version

body: That distinction is the center of the story. The evidence supports a possible **battle-system fork**, not a confirmed replacement.
## What Game Freak Actually Said

The new hook is not simply that Game Freak might change Pokemon battles. The series has already experimented. What changed is that Game Freak is now explaining why it wanted a permanent home for the old rules.

Iwao described longtime players as people who have built years of experience around a familiar Pokemon battle style. The studio does not want to simply tell those players to move on if the broader RPG series changes.

Champions solves that problem by preserving the traditional battle framework in a dedicated game. That makes it more than a battle simulator. It may function as a preservation layer for classic Pokemon combat.
English readers should treat the exact wording carefully: GCX is relying on reported translation and coverage for context, while the official Game Freak video remains the primary source.
## The Battle System Has Already Been Changing
The idea of Pokemon experimenting with combat would have sounded much more radical before the Switch era.
**Pokemon Scarlet and Violet** still use the familiar turn-based baseline for standard wild and Trainer encounters.
**Pokemon Legends: Arceus** loosened that structure. Battles could begin more directly in the field, and Agile and Strong Styles altered action speed and turn order.

**Pokemon Legends: Z-A** crossed a clearer line. The official Pokemon site describes real-time battling, with Trainers and Pokemon moving during combat while move range, timing and area of effect become tactical variables.
**Pokemon Champions** then moves in the opposite direction on purpose: it gives traditional competitive battling a persistent home.

The pattern is not traditional turns suddenly becoming real-time combat. It is traditional turns, modified turn economy, spatial real-time experimentation, and then a dedicated place for classic competitive battles.
## Why Champions Changes the Strategic Equation

Historically, each new mainline RPG had to do several jobs at once: deliver the adventure, introduce new Pokemon, support collecting, carry new mechanics and serve as the current competitive platform.
Champions separates those responsibilities.

Play! Pokemon competitions are moving to Champions, and The Pokemon Company has described Champions around traditional turn-based Pokemon battles, familiar mechanics, Singles and Doubles support, and cross-platform competitive play.

That means a future RPG may no longer need to be the only permanent home for the tournament ruleset. Designers can potentially ask what combat style fits a specific adventure instead of making every experiment carry the full weight of VGC.
This is analysis, not a confirmed Game Freak plan. But it is a meaningful structural shift.
## Does This Mean Winds & Waves Will Be Real-Time?
**No. Not based on the evidence currently available.**

Pokemon Winds and Pokemon Waves are the next new Pokemon RPG entries and are currently positioned for Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027. Their official materials emphasize a new world, islands, ocean environments and Pokemon ecosystems. They do not identify the combat format.
That silence should not be converted into evidence.

body: The strongest reading is that Game Freak is preparing for change to be possible, not that it has killed turn-based Pokemon.
## Why This Could Be One of Pokemon's Biggest Design Shifts
Pokemon battles are not just presentation. Types, Speed, switching, status effects, priority moves, held items, Abilities and prediction all grew around structured turn resolution.
Real-time or hybrid battles change what speed, range and timing mean. Legends: Z-A already shows how positioning and execution speed can become part of Pokemon combat.
For competitive players, Champions may be reassuring rather than threatening. It preserves the deep ruleset in a dedicated environment even if another RPG experiments with moment-to-moment control.
For RPG players, the separation could let Game Freak make Pokemon feel more present in the world without forcing every legacy interaction into the same adventure engine.
## Counterarguments and Uncertainties
The biggest reason not to predict an imminent turn-based departure is simple: Game Freak has not announced one for Winds & Waves.
The Legends line also does not automatically define the next paired RPGs. Z-A proves capability, not a permanent franchise rule.

Champions also has independent reasons to exist even if future RPGs remain turn-based: it lowers the barrier to competitive battling and avoids rebuilding the competitive ecosystem around a new retail title every generation.
The phrase "little by little" matters. It points just as easily toward gradual hybridization as it does toward replacement.
## GCX Verdict

**Game Freak appears to be preparing for a future in which traditional turn-based combat no longer has to be the battle system used by every major Pokemon RPG, while Pokemon Champions protects that classic system rather than replacing it.**
That is a stronger and more honest story than declaring that Winds & Waves has already abandoned turns.
## What GCX Is Watching Next
The next real evidence will be gameplay, not mood footage.

GCX will update this page when Pokemon Presents, Game Freak, The Pokemon Company or official VGC materials clarify how Winds & Waves battles work, how new Pokemon enter Champions, or whether future RPGs and Champions are meant to operate as separate battle ecosystems.

excerpt: CD Projekt Red has finally given players a release target for The Witcher 4, and the studio is making it clear that this is its biggest and most ambitious project yet.
metaDescription: CD Projekt Red says The Witcher 4 is targeting a 2028 release window. Here is what the studio confirmed about Ciri, development scale, Gamescom, and the future of the franchise.
body: # The Witcher 4 Is Targeting 2028 — CD Projekt Says Its Biggest Game Yet Will Be Worth the Wait
We finally have something more concrete than “not anytime soon.”
CD Projekt Red says **The Witcher 4 is targeting a 2028 release window**, giving players the first meaningful indication of when the next mainline Witcher game could actually arrive.
Joint CEO Michał Nowakowski shared the update on August 24 as CD Projekt prepared for Gamescom 2026. He also made one thing very clear: **The Witcher 4 will not be shown at Gamescom this year.**
The studio says more than **500 developers** are working on the game and describes it as its biggest, boldest and most ambitious project to date.
## Ciri Is Still at the Center of the New Saga
CD Projekt first revealed The Witcher 4 at The Game Awards in December 2024, confirming **Ciri as the protagonist** of the next Witcher saga.
The reveal trailer showed Ciri taking on a witcher contract in a remote village, immediately making it clear that the series is moving forward rather than simply recreating Geralt’s story.
The game is being built using customized **Unreal Engine 5** technology developed in collaboration with Epic Games.
## 2028 Is a Target, Not a Locked Release Date
The wording matters.
CD Projekt is **targeting** 2028.
That is not the same thing as announcing an exact date.
Nowakowski said the team is not ready to announce an exact date yet, so 2028 should be treated as the current goal rather than a guarantee.
## The Witcher 4 Is Not Coming to Gamescom 2026
Despite CD Projekt’s presence at Gamescom, **The Witcher 4 itself will not be shown at the event**.
Instead, the company is using Gamescom to focus attention on the broader future of the Witcher franchise.
That includes **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Songs of the Past**, the 2027 expansion bringing Geralt back for another major adventure.
That creates an unusual release bridge:

**2027:** Songs of the Past  
**2028 target:** The Witcher 4

Before today, the new Witcher 3 expansion looked like a surprising anniversary project.
Now it looks much more strategic.
CD Projekt has said Songs of the Past is intended to bring players back into the Witcher universe before the transition to Ciri in The Witcher 4.
The Witcher 3 has now sold more than **65 million copies**, giving CD Projekt a huge existing audience to reactivate before its new saga begins.
## The Scale of Development Is Massive
CD Projekt says more than 500 developers are currently working on The Witcher 4.
The studio is also juggling several other major projects, including Cyberpunk 2, the Witcher remake, Project Sirius, and its new original IP, Hadar.
The Witcher 4 remains the centerpiece.
## What About That 2025 Tech Demo?
In June 2025, CD Projekt and Epic Games showed a technology demonstration associated with The Witcher 4.
That footage was often discussed as though it were direct gameplay from the game.
CD Projekt later stressed that it was **a technology demo, not The Witcher 4 itself**.

body: # Blood of Dawnwalker Adds 60 FPS Mode After Players Push Back
That changed quickly.

After initially detailing console graphics modes that topped out at **40 FPS**, Rebel Wolves has now confirmed that **The Blood of Dawnwalker will include a Performance Mode targeting 60 FPS on Day 1**.

The new option will be available on:
- PlayStation 5
- PlayStation 5 Pro
- Xbox Series X
Xbox Series S will remain targeted at **30 FPS**.
## Rebel Wolves Says the Mode Was Already Being Tested
The developer says this was not a case of creating an entirely new mode over a weekend.
According to Rebel Wolves, Performance Mode was already in development but the team was not yet confident enough in its testing to promise it at launch.
After the initial console-performance announcement drew criticism, the studio accelerated its next round of testing.
Those results were apparently good enough to make the commitment official.
The developer says the new Performance Mode will arrive through the **Day 1 launch patch**.

body: ## Why Players Cared So Much
For a fast action RPG, frame-rate options can materially change how combat feels.
*The Blood of Dawnwalker* is built around real-time sword fighting, movement, timing and reaction speed.
Players reacting to the initial announcement were less concerned with hitting native 4K than with getting the choice to prioritize responsiveness.
That is exactly what the new Performance Mode provides.
## The Original Console Breakdown Looked Very Different

Before today’s update, Rebel Wolves had announced:
- Quality Mode: 30 FPS at dynamic 4K
- Balanced Mode: 40 FPS at dynamic 4K
That left players without the familiar performance-first option many current-generation games provide.
## Xbox Series S Is the Exception
The one console not receiving the new Performance Mode is Xbox Series S.
Rebel Wolves currently lists Series S at a **30 FPS target**.
## This Is a Smart Course Correction
Rebel Wolves says the feature was already in testing.
The community response simply made it clear that completing that testing before launch mattered.
That is exactly what pre-release communication is supposed to accomplish.
## The Bigger Question Is Whether It Holds 60 FPS
There is an important word in the announcement:
**targeting.**
The studio is not promising a locked 60 FPS in every scene.
Until independent performance analysis is available, we will not know how consistently the game can hold that target during busy combat or large environments.
## A Big September Release Just Got a Better Console Story

*The Blood of Dawnwalker* launches **September 3** for:
- PC
- PlayStation 5
- Xbox Series X|S
The game is the debut project from Rebel Wolves, founded by veterans including director **Konrad Tomaszkiewicz**, who previously served as game director on *The Witcher 3*.
The addition of a 60 FPS mode removes one of the louder pre-release concerns.
# Latest Update — August 24, 2026
Rebel Wolves has confirmed that a **Day 1 Performance Mode targeting 60 FPS** will be available on PS5, PS5 Pro, and Xbox Series X.
Xbox Series S remains targeted at 30 FPS.

body: # Every Pokémon 30th Celebration Pikachu Revealed So Far

As of this GCX snapshot, **20 of the 30 special Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Pikachu cards have been revealed**, leaving **10 still unrevealed**. Every regular 30th Celebration booster is built around the same headline hook: one of the 30 Pikachu subset cards appears in each pack.
This page is the living checklist. Routine reveals should update this URL instead of creating a new article every time another Pikachu appears.
## How the 30-Pikachu Subset Works

The 30 Pikachu are a separately numbered subset inside 30th Celebration, using `01/30` through `30/30` numbering in addition to the normal English set number. That means a card can be both `023/128` and `01/30`; GCX tracks both fields so collectors can sort the checklist correctly.

The most important rule is simple: **the 30 Pikachu are pack pulls, not product-exclusive promos**. An Elite Trainer Box Pikachu and a Booster Bundle Pikachu are not separate cards just because the pack came from a different sealed product.
## The 20 Revealed Pikachu Cards

The currently revealed cards are tracked below by subset number, English number, illustrator, visual identity and GCX editorial chase outlook. The chase labels are editorial watchlist notes, not price claims.
## Additional Pikachu ex Cards
The Day and Night Pikachu ex cards are important, but they are **outside** the 30-card Pikachu subset. GCX tracks them separately so the headline count does not get inflated.
## The 10 Pikachu Still Unrevealed

Ten subset positions remain public placeholders. Leaked artist names or checklist guesses are not treated as confirmed facts. When Pokémon reveals a card, the row moves from placeholder status to revealed status with a source and updated artwork notes.
## Early Chase Cards to Watch

Before release, the safest collector framing is prospective. The strongest early watchlist belongs to cards with distinctive artwork, major illustrator appeal or obvious anniversary-story value, not to presale listings.
## Pull Rates, Prices and Grading

One Pikachu per regular booster is the confirmed mechanic. Specific illustration odds are still unknown, so this hub does not publish a clean "1-in-30" claim for any particular design unless Pokémon or reliable post-release data supports it.
English market prices and grading populations are also not mature before retail release. Presale listings can be tracked as presale listings, but they should not be described as market value.
## FAQ
### How many Pikachu cards are in Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration?
There is a dedicated subset of 30 unique Pikachu cards. Additional Pikachu ex cards exist outside that 30-card subset.
### How many have been revealed?
GCX currently tracks 20 revealed subset Pikachu and 10 unrevealed placeholders.
### Do you get a Pikachu in every booster?
Every regular 30th Celebration booster includes one of the 30 special Pikachu cards.
### Are the Day and Night Pikachu ex cards part of the 30?
No. They are separate Pikachu ex prints and promos outside the `01/30` through `30/30` subset.
### Should GCX rank these by value yet?
Not as market fact. Until retail supply, reliable sales data and grading populations exist, rankings should remain clearly labeled as GCX editorial watchlist analysis.

title: 10 Games We're Watching Most at Gamescom 2026

excerpt: Gamescom has hundreds of games. These are the ten that could actually give us something worth talking about.
metaDescription: From The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past and Final Fantasy VII Revelation to Fable and Alien: Isolation 2, these are the 10 Gamescom 2026 games GCX is watching most closely.
body: # 10 Games We’re Watching Most at Gamescom 2026
There is a dangerous way to approach Gamescom:
Try to care about everything.
Gamescom 2026 runs **August 26–30**, with **Opening Night Live on August 25**, and the event is once again enormous.

The show floor includes more than 1,600 exhibitors, while Opening Night Live, Xbox broadcasts, the Future Games Show and individual publisher presentations will dump several days of trailers, gameplay and announcements into the same week.
We are not going to pretend every appearance deserves equal attention.
These are the **10 games GCX is watching most closely** based on franchise size, confirmed Gamescom plans and the likelihood that the event gives us something genuinely new.
Related: Gamescom 2026 Schedule & Complete Hub

body.caption: GCX is prioritizing games that have a strong reason to matter during Gamescom week, not simply the loudest names on the calendar.
rows: Playable demos
Hands-on impressions can prove whether a game feels as good as its trailers look.
Release timing
Games landing before GTA VI need to make their case quickly.
Franchise expectations
Known series like Final Fantasy, Gears and The Witcher carry built-in scrutiny.
Surprise potential
The best Gamescom stories are often the games that leave the week much bigger than they entered it.

body: # 1. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Songs of the Past
This is the easiest No. 1 on the list.
A new substantial expansion for *The Witcher 3* in 2026 would have sounded absurd a few years ago.
Now it is one of Gamescom’s headline attractions.
The expansion brings Geralt back and is expected to receive major Gamescom attention, giving us a chance to learn much more about its scope, story and place inside the larger Witcher timeline.

## What We Want
- substantial gameplay
- a clearer sense of scope
- new location details
- release timing
- pricing
- how it connects to the future of the franchise

## Standalone GCX Potential
**Extremely High**
# 2. Final Fantasy VII Revelation
Square Enix is bringing the final chapter of the *Final Fantasy VII Remake* project back into the spotlight at Opening Night Live.
That alone makes it required viewing.
The project has spent years playing with the tension between recreating the original story and deliberately changing it.
At this point, almost any substantial gameplay or story reveal has the potential to generate enormous discussion.

## What We Want
- gameplay
- world structure
- release timing
- platform details
- signs of how radically the final chapter may diverge

## Standalone GCX Potential
**Extremely High**
# 3. Gears of War: E-Day
*Gears of War: E-Day* has one advantage over a lot of Gamescom games:
People are expected to actually play it.
Xbox has positioned the game as one of its major Gamescom attractions, giving attendees a hands-on look at the campaign ahead of release.
That matters more than another polished cinematic.
We already know the game wants to revisit the horror and brutality of the earliest days of the Locust War.
Gamescom is where we start learning whether that tone actually survives once a controller is in someone’s hands.

## What We Want
- hands-on impressions
- campaign pacing
- combat feel
- horror atmosphere
- how Marcus and Dom are handled

## Standalone GCX Potential
**High**
# 4. Fable
The new *Fable* has looked gorgeous for a long time.
What it has needed is more gameplay.
Gamescom finally gives Playground Games an opportunity to prove that its version of Albion is more than beautiful scenery, good jokes and carefully edited trailers.
Xbox has indicated that Gamescom will provide more direct looks at combat and gameplay systems.
That could make this one of the most important show-floor demonstrations of the event.

## What We Want
- extended gameplay
- melee / ranged / magic combat
- exploration
- NPC interaction
- evidence that Albion feels alive outside cinematic sequences

## Standalone GCX Potential
**High**
# 5. Alien: Isolation 2
A playable sequel to *Alien: Isolation* is one of the most interesting horror stories at Gamescom.
The original game’s reputation grew around tension, vulnerability and an Alien that felt unpredictable enough to remain threatening.
A sequel cannot simply repeat the same tricks.
Gamescom gives players and press a chance to see whether Creative Assembly has found new ways to make the Xenomorph frightening again.

## What We Want
- hands-on impressions
- Alien AI behavior
- stealth systems
- level design
- how much the sequel changes the original formula

## Standalone GCX Potential
**Very High**
# 6. Silent Hill: Townfall
*Silent Hill: Townfall* has lived in mystery long enough.
Gamescom is a chance for that to change.
Konami has positioned the game for additional event coverage, and the biggest thing GCX wants is very simple:
**Gameplay.**
Atmosphere is not the question anymore.
The game needs to show us what players actually do.

## What We Want
- real gameplay
- release timing
- story premise
- how it differs from other modern Silent Hill projects

## Standalone GCX Potential
**High if substantive**
# 7. Metro 2039
The Metro series is built around details that polished trailers struggle to communicate.
Ammunition pressure. Lighting. Scavenging. Slow exploration. The feeling that the environment itself wants you dead.
That makes Gamescom hands-on impressions much more useful than another cinematic reveal.

## What We Want
- real gameplay impressions
- survival systems
- stealth
- level structure
- how the world has evolved

## Standalone GCX Potential
**Medium-High**
# 8. Persona 4 Revival
Nobody needs Gamescom to tell them *Persona 4* is a good game.
The question is what Atlus has actually changed.
The remake is expected to modernize visuals, UI, combat and quality-of-life systems while preserving the identity of Inaba and its cast.
Hands-on impressions could finally tell us how aggressive that modernization really is.

## What We Want
- combat changes
- UI changes
- exploration improvements
- new events
- comparison-worthy footage

## Standalone GCX Potential
**Medium-High**
# 9. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
*Modern Warfare 4* is already in the middle of its beta cycle.
That makes its Gamescom appearance different from most games on this list.
We do not need another introduction.
We want evidence that Activision is listening.
By Gamescom, the developers will have much more player feedback around matchmaking, movement, weapon balance and the overall beta experience.

## What We Want
- changes based on beta feedback
- multiplayer tuning
- weapon adjustments
- matchmaking commentary
- Warzone information if relevant

## Standalone GCX Potential
**Depends on the announcement**
# 10. Stranger Than Heaven
Every major showcase needs a wildcard.
For GCX, that game is *Stranger Than Heaven*.
RGG Studio’s project already looks more structurally ambitious than a simple variation on *Like a Dragon*, with a multi-era Japanese setting and an unusual combat system.
Gamescom hands-on coverage could be the moment people finally understand what this thing actually is.

## What We Want
- uninterrupted gameplay
- explanation of the multi-era structure
- combat systems
- progression
- what makes it different from RGG’s established franchises

## Standalone GCX Potential
**Sleeper**

Gamescom’s official listings include plenty of other games worth watching, including:

title: The Duskbloods Is Finally Playable - Here's What FromSoftware's Strange PvPvE Game Actually Feels Like
seoTitle: The Duskbloods Network Test: What We Learned From FromSoftware's Switch 2 Exclusive
excerpt: FromSoftware's first major Switch 2 exclusive is no longer just a mysterious trailer. The network test reveals a game built around chaos, temporary alliances, strange objectives and more player freedom than the Dark Souls battle royale label suggests.
metaDescription: The Duskbloods network test finally gives players a real look at FromSoftware's Nintendo Switch 2-exclusive PvPvE game. Here's what works, what feels strange, and what the final game still needs to prove.
body: # The Duskbloods Is Finally Playable — Here’s What FromSoftware’s Strange PvPvE Game Actually Feels Like
For more than a year, **The Duskbloods** has been one of FromSoftware’s strangest question marks.

It looks unmistakably like something from the studio behind *Dark Souls* and *Elden Ring*, but director Hidetaka Miyazaki has described it as something fundamentally different: an online-focused **PvPvE game for up to eight players**, built around changing objectives, competing incentives and supernatural characters known as the Bloodsworn of Dusk.
The closed network test running from **August 21 through August 24** has finally given players a meaningful chance to understand what that actually means.
And the answer is: this is a much stranger game than “FromSoftware makes a battle royale.”
## What The Duskbloods Actually Feels Like
Hands-on impressions published around the network test consistently describe a game that mixes recognizable FromSoftware combat with a far more chaotic match structure.
Players are not simply dropped into an arena and told to kill one another.

Matches revolve around accumulating **Virtue**, and there are multiple ways to earn it: fighting other players, defeating enemies, pursuing objectives, controlling parts of the map and completing character-specific goals.
That makes every match less predictable than a standard PvP mode.
One player may want you dead. Another may benefit from keeping you alive. A third may be pursuing a completely different objective.
That social uncertainty is one of the most interesting things the network test has revealed.
## The Combat Still Feels Like FromSoftware — But the Match Around It Does Not
The basic movement and combat language will feel familiar to anyone who has played recent FromSoftware games.
There are stamina-managed attacks, dodges, character-specific abilities and the usual emphasis on reading opponents.
But the important difference is that combat is only one part of the overall match.
Multiple previews have emphasized that players can succeed through exploration, PvE objectives, alliances and smart positioning rather than simply winning every duel.
That could make *The Duskbloods* more approachable than its intimidating premise suggests.
## The Network Test Is Only a Fraction of the Final Game
FromSoftware has confirmed that the network test does **not** represent the complete launch package.

The test includes:
- **1 of the 3 planned maps**
- **6 of the 10 planned playable characters**
The final version is also expected to include significantly more story and customization content.
Balance values, weapons, skills and the amount of Virtue awarded for different actions may also change before release.

body: ## The Match Structure Is Where Things Get Weird
One of the strongest ideas in *The Duskbloods* is that players are not always working toward the same thing.
FromSoftware has discussed systems such as **Sigils**, which can alter goals and relationships inside a match.
That can create situations where players benefit from cooperating, betraying another player, protecting someone, hunting a specific target, focusing on PvE objectives, or controlling locations.
Miyazaki has compared some of this thinking to tabletop RPGs, where players are encouraged to react to changing situations rather than follow one universal objective.
## The Final Phase Can Completely Change the Match
The network test also does not necessarily show every possible match ending.
FromSoftware has said some matches in the final game may shift into a **three-player cooperative boss encounter**.
That creates a wonderfully messy possibility: the person you were trying to kill five minutes ago might suddenly be the person you need alive.
## The First Test Also Exposed the Biggest Risk: The Servers
The first scheduled network-test session was cut short after players ran into connection problems under heavy demand.
For a traditional FromSoftware RPG, an ugly online launch is frustrating.
For *The Duskbloods*, it is existential.
The online structure is not an optional feature. It **is the game**.

body: ## What Early Impressions Agree On

### It is confusing at first
There are a lot of systems competing for attention.

### The atmosphere is classic FromSoftware
The gothic world, strange character designs and oppressive environments still look unmistakably like the studio.

### Direct combat is not everything
Players who are not elite PvP fighters can still make meaningful progress through objectives and PvE play.

### The chaos can be exciting
When player incentives collide, matches can produce situations that feel far less scripted than a traditional competitive game.

### The long-term question remains unanswered
One map and six characters are not enough to judge whether the game will stay interesting after dozens — or hundreds — of matches.
## VISUAL MODULE — What We Learned

**Core format:** 8-player PvPvE  
**Platform:** Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive  
**Network test:** Aug. 21–24, 2026  
**Launch:** 2026  
**Test content:** 1 map / 6 characters  
**Final target:** 3 maps / 10 characters  
**Biggest question:** Can its unpredictable social systems stay fun long-term?
## This Is Not Elden Ring Online
The temptation will be to evaluate *The Duskbloods* by asking whether the combat is as good as *Elden Ring*.
That matters, but it may not be the right question.
The more interesting question is whether FromSoftware can create a competitive multiplayer game where the players themselves generate memorable stories.
Temporary alliances. Unexpected betrayals. PvE bosses interrupting PvP fights. Character-specific objectives. Players who begin as enemies and end up fighting together.
That is where *The Duskbloods* appears to be taking its biggest swing.
## What The Duskbloods Still Has to Prove

- Can three maps provide enough long-term variety?
- Are ten Bloodsworn enough?
- How deep is the progression?
- How substantial is the story?
- Can the infrastructure handle launch?
## The Duskbloods Might Be FromSoftware’s Riskiest Modern Game
FromSoftware could have made another traditional Soulslike and generated enormous attention.
Instead, Miyazaki is experimenting with a game built around unpredictability.
It still has the monsters. It still has the gothic atmosphere. It still has recognizable FromSoftware combat.
But now the most unpredictable enemy in the room may be another player whose objective you do not fully understand.
That is much riskier.
It is also why *The Duskbloods* is suddenly one of the most interesting games on Nintendo Switch 2.
# Latest Update — August 24, 2026
The final scheduled *Duskbloods* network-test window concludes August 24.
Nintendo and FromSoftware still list the game for release in **2026** exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2.

Gamescom 2026 is shaping up to be one of the biggest remaining gaming events of the year.

body: # Pokemon 30th Celebration Has a Lot More Than One Release Day
Pokemon TCG: **30th Celebration** officially begins releasing worldwide on **September 16, 2026**, but collectors will not be able to buy every product on day one.

The Pokemon Company has confirmed multiple waves extending into October, November and December, including the standard Elite Trainer Box, Booster Bundle, Mini Tins, premium collections and the massive Day and Night Ultra-Premium Collections.

That makes MSRP especially important. High-demand Pokemon products routinely appear online above their intended retail prices before launch, and 30th Celebration is already attracting enough attention that collectors should know the difference between **MSRP** and somebody simply asking for more money.
GCX will keep this page updated as additional retailer inventory and preorder drops appear.

* **Best pack value:** Booster Bundle at $26.94 for six packs, or about $4.49 per pack.
* **Most compelling ETB:** Pokemon Center ETB, if you can get it at $59.99 MSRP.
* **Biggest premium-risk product:** Day/Night Ultra-Premium Collection at $179.99 MSRP.

body: # Best Value: The Booster Bundle

For collectors who mostly want to open packs, the **Booster Bundle currently looks like the cleanest value in the lineup**. It includes **six booster packs** at an MSRP of **$26.94**, which works out to roughly **$4.49 per pack**.

There are no extra promos or accessories inflating the price, so the Booster Bundle is basically the straightforward "I just want packs" option. The downside is timing: it does not arrive until more than two weeks after the first 30th Celebration products.
# Standard ETB vs. Pokemon Center ETB

body: For only a $10 MSRP difference, the Pokemon Center version adds two packs **and** the exclusive stamped promo. If you can actually purchase one from Pokemon Center at retail price, it is arguably the more compelling collector product.
# The $179.99 Ultra-Premium Collection Is the Big One
The **30th Celebration Day and Night Ultra-Premium Collections** launch November 6 at an expected U.S. MSRP of **$179.99**.

Current product information shows the package containing **29 standard 30th Celebration booster packs**, **one Classic Collection booster pack**, Pikachu ex and either Espeon ex or Umbreon ex content depending on the version, plus a playmat, sleeves, deck box and additional accessories.

At $179.99, this clearly is not the budget option. But the Classic Collection pack makes it different from simply buying a stack of Booster Bundles. This will probably be one of the products where collectors need to be especially careful with preorder premiums.

30th Celebration is unquestionably a high-interest set, but it also has an unusually broad product lineup releasing across several months. Collectors should be particularly cautious about paying large premiums months before release unless scarcity becomes much clearer.

Several products begin at only **$9.99**. The 2-Pack Blister, Knock Out Collection and Day & Night Mini Tins all sit at that price level, with each containing two booster packs.

body: # Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Is Looking Like One of the Biggest Collector Sets in Years
Thirty different Pikachu cards.
A brand-new rarity.
Classic cards spanning the history of the Pokémon Trading Card Game.
Mew. Mewtwo. Charizard. Lugia. Ho-Oh. Umbreon. Espeon.
And an absolutely enormous lineup of sealed products arriving across several release waves.
Pokémon could have celebrated the Trading Card Game's 30th anniversary with a nostalgic mini-set and a commemorative Elite Trainer Box.
Instead, **Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration** is starting to look like one of the company's biggest collector-focused releases in years.

The expansion launches worldwide on **September 16, 2026**, becoming the first Pokémon TCG expansion to receive a simultaneous global release. Every card inside a standard booster pack will be foil, every pack will contain one of 30 unique Pikachu cards, and a new Futuristic Rare card treatment will debut alongside a Classic Collection celebrating cards from throughout the game's three-decade history.
And Pokémon is still revealing cards.
That means this hub isn't finished.
We'll continue updating it as new cards, products, preorder information and availability details are confirmed.
## When Does Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Release?
The primary release date for **Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration is September 16, 2026**.

Unlike most Pokémon TCG releases, which historically haven't always launched at exactly the same time across every market, Pokémon says 30th Celebration will be the **first expansion released simultaneously worldwide**.
Not every product arrives September 16, however.
Pokémon is spreading the anniversary lineup across four major waves:

* **September 16, 2026 — Main launch**
* **October 2, 2026 — Booster Bundle, Binder Collection and Mini Tins**
* **October 30, 2026 — Espeon ex and Umbreon ex Battle Decks**
* **November 6, 2026 — Ultra-Premium Collections, Mew/Mewtwo Figure Collections and Ditto Premium Collection**
That staggered schedule means 30th Celebration will likely remain a major Pokémon TCG story for months rather than disappearing after launch weekend.

body: # Every Booster Pack Has a Pikachu
The defining feature of 30th Celebration may be its army of Pikachu.
Every standard booster contains:

* **5 foil Pokémon TCG cards**
* **1 foil Basic Energy**
* **1 of 30 different Pikachu cards guaranteed among those five cards**
All of the cards in the expansion are foil.
That means Pokémon has essentially hidden a second collecting challenge inside the overall expansion.
Completing the entire set is one goal.
Completing **all 30 Pikachu** is another.
# Every 30th Celebration Pikachu Revealed So Far

GCX is now tracking the 30-card Pikachu subset in a dedicated living checklist. **20 of 30 Pikachu cards have been revealed so far**, one appears in every regular 30th Celebration booster, and 10 remain unrevealed.
Read the full visual checklist here: [Every Pokémon 30th Celebration Pikachu Revealed So Far](article.html?id=gcx-newsroom-pokemon-30th-celebration-pikachu-cards).

Pokémon has been revealing the illustrations gradually, with the cards depicting Pikachu in dramatically different situations and artistic styles. Officially revealed examples range from Pikachu lounging among pillows to stuffing its cheeks with Berries and sprinting across brightly colored landscapes.
The strategy is clever because it creates an easy collecting objective even for people who have no intention of completing the full expansion.
