body: Thirty Pikachu is a lot.
But it's also just achievable enough to make collectors think:
*I could probably do that.*
Famous last words.
# The Pikachu Cards Are Already Generating Serious Collector Interest
Community reaction suggests Pokémon may have found the centerpiece it was looking for.

A Reddit post showcasing leaked images of several anniversary Pikachu illustrations drew more than **1,700 upvotes** in less than a week, with collectors already picking favorites and talking about attempting a complete Pikachu subset.
That's useful as an interest signal, although leaked card images should never be treated as official confirmation until Pokémon publicly reveals the cards.
The broader takeaway is much safer:
**Collectors care about these Pikachu.**
And because Pokémon is revealing them gradually rather than dumping all 30 designs at once, every new group creates another mini-event leading toward launch.
### Current newsroom assessment
**Collector-interest level: Extremely High**
This may ultimately be one of the most recognizable subsets of the entire 30th Celebration release.
# Pokémon Is Introducing a Brand-New Rarity: Futuristic Rare
30th Celebration isn't looking exclusively backward.
Pokémon is also introducing a new **Futuristic Rare** card rarity designed to represent the future of the Pokémon TCG.
The first confirmed Futuristic Rare cards feature **Mew and Mewtwo**, with artwork from Japanese artist **YOSHIROTTEN**.
The choice of Mew and Mewtwo is pretty hard to argue with.

They're two of the most recognizable Pokémon from the franchise's original generation, but their futuristic treatment allows the anniversary expansion to use them as a bridge between Pokémon's past and whatever visual direction comes next.
That past-present-future theme runs throughout 30th Celebration.
The Pikachu cards celebrate the present through dozens of contemporary artists.
Futuristic Rares look forward.
And the Classic Collection goes straight for the nostalgia jugular.
# What Is the 30th Celebration Classic Collection?
The **Classic Collection** brings notable Pokémon cards from previous eras back into the anniversary set.
Pokémon has already confirmed examples including:

* **Charizard from Base Set**
* **Pikachu & Zekrom-GX from Sun & Moon—Team Up**
These aren't simply new cards that happen to feature the same Pokémon. They're commemorative returns of recognizable cards from Pokémon TCG history.

Pokémon has also clarified that these reprints aren't automatically legal in the Standard format. Their legality depends on whether the underlying original card is permitted in the format being played.
For collectors, though, tournament legality probably isn't the main attraction.
This is about nostalgia.
The Pokémon TCG has existed long enough that multiple generations of players have their own defining era.
For one collector, that might be Base Set Charizard.
For another, Neo-era Lugia.
For someone younger, it might be an iconic Tag Team card.
A 30th-anniversary collection gives Pokémon the opportunity to hit all of those nostalgia buttons at once.
# Lugia and Ho-Oh Join 30th Celebration
One of the latest official reveals brings **Lugia and Ho-Oh** into the set.

Pokémon revealed the Johto Legendary pair on August 19, while specialist Pokémon TCG outlet PokéBeach noted that Lugia's attack deliberately calls back to the famous Lugia released in **Neo Genesis in 2000**.
That's the sort of design detail that makes this anniversary release more interesting than a collection of popular Pokémon with a “30” logo slapped onto them.
Pokémon is deliberately referencing its own TCG history.
For longtime collectors, those callbacks may be as important as the card artwork itself.
# The Legendary Pokémon Reveals Keep Coming
The last week alone has brought a substantial number of recognizable Legendary Pokémon into the set.
Recent reveals include:
### Lugia and Ho-Oh
Revealed August 19. Lugia includes a clear callback to its Neo Genesis predecessor.
### Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres
The original Legendary birds were officially revealed together, along with another anniversary Pikachu design.
### Kyogre and Groudon
The legendary rivals from Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire were revealed on August 20.
### Zacian and Zamazenta
The Sword and Shield mascots were revealed alongside Kyogre and Groudon.
### Reshiram and Zekrom
The Unova Legendary pair has also been revealed, alongside Unown and Drifloon.
That mix reinforces one of the expansion's strongest ideas:
30th Celebration isn't tied to one Pokémon generation.
It's attempting to represent **30 years of the franchise**.
# Day and Night Pikachu ex Could Become Major Chase Cards
Two of the cards we're watching most closely are the special illustration rare versions of **Pikachu ex** built around the set's Day and Night theme.
Pokémon and PokéBeach revealed the pair in mid-August, with the artworks corresponding to the broader day/night aesthetic being used throughout several 30th Celebration products.
That theme eventually extends into the two Ultra-Premium Collections releasing in November:
**Day:** Pikachu ex + Espeon ex
**Night:** Pikachu ex + Umbreon ex
Given Pikachu's popularity and the enormous collector following surrounding both Umbreon and Espeon, those products and associated cards are obvious early candidates for heavy demand.
That does **not** mean they are guaranteed to become the most valuable cards in the expansion.
Pre-release “chase card” predictions have a nasty habit of being wrong.
But from a collector-interest standpoint, they're among the cards we'll be monitoring most closely.
# More Than 160 Cards Are Coming
Pokémon hasn't yet published a final complete checklist through its official card database, but we do have one useful clue about the overall size of the expansion.
The 30th Celebration Poster Collection contains a poster displaying images of **more than 160 cards from the expansion**.
That establishes something important:
This is not a tiny anniversary mini-set.

With more than 160 images represented on the poster, 30 Pikachu variations, classic cards, illustration rares, Pokémon ex and new rarity treatments, collectors should expect a substantial master-set challenge.
We'll add the complete numbered checklist here once Pokémon officially publishes it.
# Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Products
The product lineup is enormous.
Instead of releasing a couple of boxes on September 16, Pokémon is extending 30th Celebration across September, October and November.
Here's the confirmed U.S. schedule so far.
## September 16 — Launch Day
### 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box
The standard Elite Trainer Box contains:

* 9 30th Celebration booster packs
* Full-art Nidorina promo
* 16 foil Basic Energy cards
* 65 card sleeves
* Player's booklet
* Damage-counter dice
* Coin-flip die
* Plastic coin
* Storage box and dividers
* Pokémon TCG Live code card
The Nidorina choice isn't random: Nidorina is **Pokédex #0030**, a cute little anniversary detail that fits the theme perfectly.
## Pokémon Center Elite Trainer Box
The Pokémon Center-exclusive version increases the pack count to **11 boosters** and contains two Nidorina promos, including one stamped with the Pokémon Center logo.
For sealed-product collectors, the stamped promo alone could make the Pokémon Center version significantly more desirable than the standard ETB.
## Tech Sticker Collection
Available with either:

* Alolan Exeggutor
* Lucario
Each collection includes a corresponding promo, a tech-sticker sheet and **three 30th Celebration booster packs**.
## Poster Collection
This one may be surprisingly useful for collectors.
It includes:

* Articuno promo
* Zapdos promo
* Moltres promo
* 3 booster packs
* Poster displaying artwork from more than 160 cards in the expansion
That poster could essentially become an old-school physical checklist for anyone attempting a master set.
## Sylveon ex and Greninja ex Boxes
Each version contains:

* Sylveon ex or Greninja ex promo
* Oversize version of that card
* 4 booster packs
Both arrive September 16.
## 2-Pack Blister
The two-pack blister includes:

* 2 booster packs
* Eevee foil card
* Plastic coin
## Knock Out Collection
Another smaller launch-day option featuring:

* Eevee foil card
* Plastic coin
* 2 booster packs
# October 2 — The Pack-Opening Wave
Collectors mainly interested in opening packs may want to pay close attention to the second wave.
## Booster Bundle
The Booster Bundle contains **six 30th Celebration packs** without the accessories found in larger collection boxes.
If these remain readily available at normal retail pricing, they may become one of the simplest ways to open the set.
## Binder Collection
The Binder Collection contains:

* 9-pocket anniversary binder
* 5 booster packs
It arrives October 2 in the United States.
For anyone seriously attempting those 30 Pikachu cards, Pokémon selling you the binder to put them in feels almost suspiciously convenient.
## Mini Tins
Ten Mini Tin designs will be available.
Each includes:

* 2 booster packs
* Sticker sheet
* Art card
The ten collectible artworks combine to create two larger Day and Night images.
So naturally, there is another collection inside the collection inside the collection.
Pokémon has mastered this.
# October 30 — Espeon and Umbreon Battle Decks
Two all-foil 60-card Battle Decks arrive October 30.
One is centered around **Espeon ex**, while the other stars **Umbreon ex**.
Each includes the complete playable deck plus accessories, with Victini paired with the Espeon deck and Zeraora featured alongside Umbreon.
Umbreon products tend to attract attention almost automatically, so the Night-themed side of this anniversary lineup is going to be particularly interesting to watch.
# November 6 — The Premium Wave
If September is the launch and October is the pack-opening phase, November is where Pokémon comes after the collectors who still have money left.
Good luck to all involved.
## Day and Night Ultra-Premium Collections
There are two versions.
### Day Ultra-Premium Collection
Features:

* Pikachu ex promo
* Espeon ex promo
* Day-themed playmat
* Card sleeves
* Deck box
* Espeon coin
* Dice
* **29 standard 30th Celebration booster packs**
* **1 Classic Collection booster containing 3 Classic Collection cards**
### Night Ultra-Premium Collection
Uses the same structure but swaps Espeon for **Umbreon** and uses Night-themed artwork and accessories.
Thirty total packs in a single product makes these some of the largest boxes in the entire anniversary lineup.
They're also especially notable because the included special booster guarantees **three Classic Collection cards**.
We expect these UPCs to be among the most watched sealed products of the entire anniversary.
# Mew and Mewtwo Figure Collections
Also arriving November 6 are separate figure collections featuring Mew or Mewtwo.
Each includes:

* Mew or Mewtwo promo
* Oversize version of the card
* Sculpted figure
* 5 booster packs
Combined with the Futuristic Rare cards, Pokémon is giving both Mew and Mewtwo substantial representation throughout the anniversary release.
# Ditto Premium Collection
Ditto gets its own premium box as well.
The collection includes a Ditto promo, a colorful acrylic display and **eight 30th Celebration booster packs**.
# Which 30th Celebration Products Look Most Interesting?
We need actual retail pricing and real-world availability before making definitive value judgments, but based purely on confirmed contents, several products immediately stand out.
## Best for opening packs: Booster Bundle
Six packs.
No giant box filled with accessories you may not want.
Assuming normal pricing and reasonable availability, this should be one of the cleanest ways to open the expansion.
## Best launch-day collector product: Pokémon Center ETB
The additional packs are nice.
The exclusive stamped Nidorina promo is the bigger attraction.
Pokémon Center-exclusive ETBs have become collector targets in their own right, and the 30th-anniversary branding gives this one obvious long-term appeal.
## Most ambitious product: Day/Night UPCs
Thirty packs.
Classic Collection cards.
Pikachu.
Espeon or Umbreon.
Exclusive accessories.
These aren't subtle products.
They're designed to be centerpiece purchases.
The biggest question won't be whether collectors want them.
It'll be whether they can find them at a reasonable price.
# Should You Pay Huge Presale Prices for 30th Celebration?
Our early answer:
**Be very careful.**
Community discussion around 30th Celebration already shows substantial anxiety over availability, preorder access and inflated prices.

Reddit threads are full of collectors asking how Pokémon Center preorders work, whether Classic Collection cards are effectively locked behind expensive premium products, and whether they'll be able to purchase products without paying secondary-market prices.
Those discussions tell us demand is high.
They do **not** tell us actual post-release scarcity.
That's an important distinction.
A hot presale market can convince buyers that they need to pay an enormous premium before a product has even reached normal retail shelves.
Sometimes that fear proves justified.
Sometimes additional supply arrives and those early buyers dramatically overpay.
Until we know more about U.S. allocation and restock patterns, collectors should be cautious about treating inflated early listings as the “real” price of these products.
We'll add a dedicated MSRP and availability tracker to this hub as confirmed retail pricing becomes clearer.
# What Could Be the Biggest Chase Cards?
It's far too early to rank the final chase cards with confidence.
But several obvious candidates have already emerged based on character popularity, treatment and collector reaction.
### Pikachu ex — Day
Special illustration rare treatment combined with the anniversary mascot.
### Pikachu ex — Night
Same logic, with the Night artwork carrying additional appeal from the associated Umbreon theme.
### Mew Futuristic Rare
New rarity + iconic Pokémon + YOSHIROTTEN artwork.
### Mewtwo Futuristic Rare
Potentially one of the defining cards of the new Futuristic Rare treatment.
### Lugia
Historical callback to one of Pokémon TCG's best-known older cards.
### Charizard Classic Collection
It's Charizard.
We could probably end the analysis there.
Still, none of these should be described as the definitive “most valuable” card before real pull rates and market transactions exist.
The smartest thing our newsroom can do is track the market instead of pretending to predict it perfectly.
# Why 30th Celebration Feels Different
Anniversary Pokémon sets aren't unusual.
What makes 30th Celebration interesting is how many different collector instincts Pokémon is targeting simultaneously.
### Nostalgia
Historic cards return through the Classic Collection.
### Completion
Thirty Pikachu give collectors a clearly defined subset to chase.
### Modern artwork
Illustration rares and special illustration rares appeal to the modern Pokémon collector.
### Novelty
Futuristic Rare gives the set something genuinely new.
### Character popularity
Pikachu, Mew, Mewtwo, Charizard, Umbreon, Espeon, Lugia, Ho-Oh, Sylveon and Greninja barely scratch the surface.
### Sealed collecting
ETBs, Pokémon Center exclusives, Mini Tins, two UPCs and themed boxes give sealed collectors plenty to hunt.
### Multiple generations
Instead of focusing exclusively on 1996 nostalgia, the set references Pokémon history across multiple eras.
That's important.
Someone who started collecting in 1999 and someone who started in 2019 can both find nostalgia here.
# Is Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Worth Collecting?
We can't fully answer that until the set releases.
But based on everything Pokémon has officially announced so far, **30th Celebration looks like one of the most significant collector-focused Pokémon TCG releases of 2026**.
The 30 Pikachu concept gives it an instantly recognizable identity.
Classic Collection provides history.
Futuristic Rare provides novelty.
The product lineup creates multiple entry points.
And the steady stream of card reveals is keeping collector attention unusually high more than three weeks before release.
There's still plenty we don't know.
We don't have the final official checklist.
We don't have real pull-rate data.
We don't know how plentiful product will actually be at launch.
We don't know which cards will command the highest prices after the market settles.
And we definitely don't know whether today's eye-watering presale prices will look reasonable or ridiculous six months from now.
That's why this hub will remain active.
# Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration FAQ
## When does Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration release?
The main expansion launches **September 16, 2026**, with additional products releasing October 2, October 30 and November 6.
## How many cards are in each booster pack?
Each booster contains **five foil cards plus one foil Basic Energy card**. One of the five cards is guaranteed to be one of the 30 Pikachu designs.
## Are all 30th Celebration cards foil?
Yes. Pokémon says every card in the expansion is foil, including Basic Energy.
## How many Pikachu cards are in 30th Celebration?
There are **30 unique Pikachu cards** specifically built around the anniversary concept, and every booster pack guarantees one.
## What is Futuristic Rare?
Futuristic Rare is a new rarity debuting in 30th Celebration. Mew and Mewtwo are among the first confirmed cards using the treatment, with artwork by YOSHIROTTEN.
## Is Base Set Charizard coming back?
Yes. Pokémon has officially shown the Base Set Charizard as part of the anniversary's classic-card component.
## Will 30th Celebration have booster boxes?
Pokémon has announced Booster Bundles and numerous collection products but has not announced a conventional 36-pack booster box as part of the U.S. product lineup currently published.
## When do the Ultra-Premium Collections release?
Both Day and Night Ultra-Premium Collections launch **November 6, 2026**.
## How many packs are in the 30th Celebration UPC?
Each UPC contains **29 normal boosters plus one Classic Collection booster containing three Classic Collection cards**.
## Should I preorder at inflated secondary-market prices?

Demand is clearly strong, but final availability is not yet known. Paying a large premium before normal retail distribution begins carries substantial risk. We recommend comparing listings against confirmed retail pricing and waiting for clearer supply information whenever possible.

title: GTA VI Is Leaking Again - Just Days Before Rockstar's Biggest Official Look Yet
excerpt: Purported GTA VI gameplay footage has appeared online less than two weeks before Rockstar is scheduled to finally give players an extended official look at the game.
body: Rockstar Games has spent years controlling almost every meaningful glimpse of Grand Theft Auto VI. This week, that control appears to have slipped again.

Several videos purportedly showing GTA VI gameplay began circulating online on August 18, including footage appearing to show protagonist Jason Duval moving through the world, driving vehicles and taking part in various activities. Some of the material has already been removed following copyright complaints, although Rockstar has not publicly confirmed that the footage is authentic.

That distinction matters. Until Rockstar identifies the material as legitimate, anything shown in the leaked footage should be treated as unverified rather than as a confirmed list of GTA VI features.
Still, the timing could hardly be more dramatic.

Rockstar has already announced that Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look will premiere on August 27 at 3 p.m. ET through Netflix and Rockstar's official channels. The game itself remains scheduled for November 19, 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
That means Rockstar was only days away from giving players the deeper look they have been waiting for.

For years, almost every scrap of GTA VI information has generated enormous attention. But leaked development footage presents a problem: without knowing when footage was captured, what build it came from or whether specific systems remained intact during development, individual details can easily be misinterpreted.

The new material reportedly includes glimpses of gameplay systems and locations, while other circulating material claims to show a broader look at Leonida's map. Those claims should remain firmly in the rumor column until Rockstar confirms them.
The August 27 presentation is therefore becoming more important, not less.

Rockstar now has an opportunity to show GTA VI exactly as it wants players to see it: finished gameplay systems, deliberate camera work, properly presented environments and whatever surprises the company has deliberately held back.

rows: Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled for November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

body: This is not the first time Rockstar's secrecy around GTA VI has been broken. A massive 2022 breach exposed development footage years before the game was ready to be shown publicly, creating one of the most notorious leaks in gaming history.

Four years later, the circumstances are different. GTA VI is no longer a distant project pieced together through rumors. Preorders are underway, its November release is approaching, and Rockstar is preparing to open the information floodgates.

That is why leak coverage needs a different tone now. The useful question is not whether a random clip looks exciting in isolation. It is how much clearer the official extended look makes the final game feel once Rockstar controls the presentation, image quality and context.
That makes these latest leaks less of a first look at GTA VI and more of an unexpected appetizer immediately before the main course. August 27 is now appointment viewing.

title: Gamescom 2026 Could Be the Last Huge Gaming Showcase Before GTA VI Takes Over
excerpt: Gamescom returns next week with Xbox broadcasts, Opening Night Live and an enormous slate of upcoming games competing for attention during one of the busiest release seasons in years.
body: The gaming industry is about to descend on Cologne.
Gamescom 2026 officially runs August 26 through August 30, while Geoff Keighley's Opening Night Live kicks off the major public-facing announcements one day earlier on August 25.
Normally, that is enough to make Gamescom one of the biggest weeks of the gaming calendar. This year feels different.
An enormous number of high-profile games are preparing to launch over the next several months, and sitting near the end of that calendar is Grand Theft Auto VI, currently scheduled for November 19.
For publishers trying to convince players that their game deserves attention this fall, Gamescom suddenly matters quite a bit.

Opening Night Live begins August 25 at 2 p.m. ET and serves as the week's major kickoff event. Gamescom then transitions into days of publisher broadcasts, demonstrations, interviews and playable games on the Cologne show floor.

Xbox has two broadcasts scheduled for August 26 and 27, while the Future Games Show is scheduled for August 26. Expected showcases and publisher streams give the week a dense calendar even before surprises are counted.
That is usually where Gamescom becomes dangerous for anyone trying to maintain a reasonable gaming backlog. One good trailer turns into three. Three turn into twelve. Suddenly October costs $600.
There is another reason Gamescom feels particularly important in 2026: Rockstar is about to accelerate its own marketing.
GTA VI gets an official extended presentation on August 27, right in the middle of Gamescom week, before launching November 19. That is an extraordinary amount of gravitational pull for one game.
Publishers launching titles in September, October and early November effectively have a limited window to establish their games before the GTA VI conversation becomes almost impossible to escape.

A game that enters the week as something players saw once can leave Cologne sitting near the top of millions of wishlists. That is why the most interesting part of Gamescom may not be the expected blockbusters. It may be discovering the game nobody had circled before the show began.

What matters is whether Gamescom produces a handful of moments that materially change how players view upcoming games: a great gameplay demonstration, a surprise release date, a previously unknown project, or a struggling game suddenly looking fantastic.

Gamescom 2026 has hundreds of companies fighting for attention during a year when one of the most anticipated videogames ever made is approaching from the other side of the calendar. The fight to get noticed starts August 25.

Whether the kickoff produces a few clear breakout trailers rather than a blur of reveals.

GTA VI extended look

title: Phantom Blade Zero Finally Showed Us What Exists Beyond Those Ridiculous Sword Fights
excerpt: S-Game's latest Phantom Blade Zero presentation revealed a much larger action RPG hiding behind the spectacular combat clips that originally made the game famous.
body: For the last several years, Phantom Blade Zero has been remarkably easy to describe. It was the game with the insane sword fighting. Then S-Game showed us the rest of it.

The August 17 Phantom Blade Zero State of Play offered the deepest look yet at the game's world, RPG systems, weapon customization, side quests and difficulty options. Suddenly this looks much more ambitious than a collection of gorgeous boss fights connected by hallways.
Combat remains the obvious centerpiece.

Players will be able to unlock more than 30 main weapons and 25 secondary weapons called Phantom Edges. Weapons can be upgraded and paired with accessories, while defeated enemies can expand the player's arsenal. S-Game also says players can reforge upgraded equipment to recover materials and invest them elsewhere.

That is a lot more build flexibility than the game's early trailers suggested. Rather than forcing everyone toward one hyper-specific parry-and-counter playstyle, S-Game is promising ranged options, summons and different ways to construct Soul's combat loadout.
The sword fighting still looks absurd. Now it appears to have an RPG underneath it.
The bigger surprise is how exploration works.
S-Game describes the Wulin as an interconnected martial-arts world filled with settlements, dangerous regions, side quests and secrets. Some optional quests can even create additional story paths.
Rather than one giant conventional open world, the presentation suggests connected areas with hand-painted, Chinese ink-wash-style maps. That sounds like a potentially smart compromise.

Open-world fatigue is real. Not every action game benefits from having 200 icons scattered across an enormous map. Phantom Blade Zero appears more interested in building dense areas that connect together while still giving players meaningful room to explore.

body.caption: The State of Play shifted Phantom Blade Zero from a combat-showcase game into something closer to a full action-RPG pitch.
rows: Weapons
More than 30 main weapons and 20-plus Phantom Edges point to build variety rather than one fixed sword style.
Exploration
The Wulin is being framed as connected regions with settlements, secrets and optional quest paths.
Difficulty
Multiple settings suggest the game wants stylish mastery without locking out players who mainly want the story.
Martial-arts direction
Donnie Yen's involvement gives the action a clearer cinematic reference point.

body: Another interesting choice is difficulty. S-Game revealed multiple settings ranging from a story-friendly option to harsher challenge modes. That is notable because Phantom Blade Zero's visual language practically screams that it will punish players.
Providing multiple difficulty options could give the game a considerably broader audience than its brutal-looking combat initially suggested.
S-Game also confirmed a significant role for martial-arts icon Donnie Yen, who serves as a creative consultant and provides facial and motion capture for Mo Yuan.
For a game leaning this heavily into martial-arts cinema, having someone with Yen's experience involved in how the action looks and moves is a genuinely interesting creative choice.
The combat got everyone's attention. The latest presentation finally gave players a reason to care about everything happening between the fights.

title: Horizon Hunters Gathering Is Reportedly Being Reworked - and Sony's Live-Service Strategy Looks Different Again
excerpt: A new report says Guerrilla's Horizon multiplayer game is losing much of its live-service structure after disappointing private testing.
body: Sony's complicated experiment with live-service games may be changing again.
Horizon Hunters Gathering, Guerrilla Games' cooperative spin-off set in the Horizon universe, is reportedly undergoing a significant overhaul after receiving poor feedback during private testing.

According to reporting attributed to Bloomberg and subsequently detailed by VGC, Guerrilla is removing much of the game's live-service structure and repositioning it as a smaller, more traditional cooperative multiplayer game with a story component.
Sony has not publicly announced the reported overhaul, so those details should currently be treated as reported development information rather than an official change in direction.
First: the game reportedly has not been canceled.

Reports indicate remaining developers have until December 2026 to demonstrate to Sony executives that the project should continue active development. Many staff members assigned to the game are also reportedly being transferred to another project.
That puts Hunters Gathering in an unusual position. It is alive, but apparently fighting for its life.
The game was announced earlier this year as a tactical co-op action game that could be played either alongside other players or solo with NPC companions. Now its entire identity may be shifting.
If this were happening in isolation, it would simply be a story about one project having a difficult development cycle. It is not happening in isolation.

Sony publicly pursued an aggressive expansion into live-service games earlier in the generation. That strategy produced an enormous success with Helldivers 2, but it also produced one of PlayStation's most infamous failures in Concord, which was pulled from sale only weeks after release.

That is what makes the reported Horizon overhaul interesting. Sony does not necessarily appear to be abandoning multiplayer. It appears to be becoming much more selective about what kind of multiplayer games it is willing to ship.
# What Is Official vs. What Is Reported

The official version of *Horizon Hunters Gathering* is still a PS5 and PC co-op action game from Guerrilla, built around three-player machine hunts, tactical combat, replayable missions, a social hub, and a narrative campaign set inside the Horizon universe.

The reported version of the story is the possible change in direction. VGC, citing Bloomberg, says Sony and Guerrilla are reworking the project after private testing, stripping out much of the live-service framework and aiming for a more traditional co-op game with a smaller scope.

body: There is an intriguing game buried inside the basic idea. The Horizon universe already revolves around coordinated hunts against enormous machines, elemental weaknesses, traps, specialized weapons and enemies that behave differently depending on which components players destroy.
That is almost begging for cooperative play. It does not inherently need an endless seasonal treadmill wrapped around it.

A smaller co-op game built around great hunts, a meaningful campaign and strong replayability could conceivably fit Horizon better than a product designed primarily around long-term engagement metrics.
# Why a Smaller Co-op Horizon Could Make Sense

Horizon combat already has the pieces of a strong cooperative loop. One player can expose armor plates, another can set traps, and a third can punish elemental weaknesses or control space while the machine changes behavior under pressure.

That fantasy is easier to understand than a broad service game trying to become a new daily habit. If the rework is real, the opportunity is to make *Hunters Gathering* feel like focused, repeatable hunting missions rather than a platform that needs endless seasonal scaffolding from day one.

The risk is that a smaller scope can also mean uncertainty: fewer modes, a narrower launch plan, and less room for the kind of long-term updates that multiplayer communities expect. Sony and Guerrilla will need to show whether this is a sharper creative pivot or simply a rescue attempt.
# What Readers Should Watch Next

The next useful update will be an official development blog, new trailer, public beta date, or platform-store update that confirms whether the game's pitch has changed. Until then, the safest read is that *Horizon Hunters Gathering* remains announced, but its final shape is still in motion.
Whether that is actually what Guerrilla is building remains unknown. The reported December evaluation is the next milestone to watch.

title: A $1,000 PS6 Sounds Absurd - New Analysis Shows Why It Could Be a Disaster
excerpt: Nobody has announced a $1,000 PlayStation 6 or next-generation Xbox. But one research firm's worst-case scenario shows why hardware prices are becoming one of gaming's biggest problems.
body: Before anyone starts panic-selling their PS5: Sony has not announced that the PlayStation 6 will cost $1,000. Microsoft has not announced a $1,000 next-generation Xbox either.
What we do have is a newly published scenario from Ampere Analysis examining what could happen if conventional next-generation PlayStation and Xbox systems launch around 2028 at that price.
The answer is simple: a whole lot fewer people may buy them.

Ampere's model estimates that combined PS6 and next-generation Xbox sales during their first five years could be as much as 38% lower than comparable PS5 and Xbox Series X|S sales if the new systems launch at $1,000.
That is not a prediction that $1,000 consoles are definitely happening. It is a warning about what happens if they do.

body.caption: The important distinction: this is scenario analysis, not a confirmed next-generation price announcement.
rows: $1,000 conventional next-generation PlayStation and Xbox systems around 2028.
A high price could shrink early adoption before the software ecosystem has time to compound.
Up to 38% lower combined hardware sales over the first five years.
Fewer console owners also means fewer potential buyers for games, subscriptions, DLC and accessories.
A games-and-services market billions of dollars smaller by 2031 under the higher-price scenario.
The risk is not just launch-week backlash; it is a smaller addressable console audience over years.
No official PS6 or next Xbox price has been announced.
The article should stay framed as pricing-risk analysis, not hardware rumor confirmation.

body: The real problem is not only selling the console. It is everything that comes afterward.

According to the scenario, a $1,000 hardware environment could leave PlayStation and Xbox's combined games-and-services market billions of dollars smaller by 2031 than under a scenario where systems sell closer to $700.

Console manufacturers do not just want to sell a box. They want that box sitting under a television for seven years while players buy games, subscriptions, DLC, microtransactions, accessories and eventually another controller.
A customer who never buys the console generates none of that downstream revenue. At some point, raising hardware prices can actually make the ecosystem less valuable.

The reason $1,000 is even being discussed is that components have become painfully expensive. Continuing component shortages, tariffs, trade pressures and broader hardware costs have changed the math around console pricing.
The next console generation has a math problem, and nobody has solved it yet.

There are ways out. Sony and Microsoft could delay the next generation and hope component economics improve. They could launch on schedule while subsidizing hardware more aggressively. Or they could rethink what a console generation needs to be.
That third option may ultimately be the most interesting.

body.caption: If next-generation hardware economics get ugly, platform holders have several imperfect options.
rows: Delay the next console cycle.
Keeps prices from shocking buyers immediately, but risks making the current generation feel stretched.
Subsidize hardware more aggressively.
Protects adoption, but increases pressure to earn money through software, subscriptions and digital stores.
Push digital-only or modular hardware.
Can reduce manufacturing cost, but may frustrate players who still value physical media and ownership flexibility.
Rethink the generational leap.
A less conventional device could avoid a pure graphics-power arms race, but it requires a much clearer value proposition.

body: For decades, console generations have been sold using essentially the same argument: look how much better the graphics are. But if producing another enormous graphical leap requires building a $1,000 machine, consumers may finally respond by keeping the hardware they already own.
The next console war might not be decided by who builds the most powerful box. It might be decided by who figures out how to build one normal people can still afford.
